pairs.note: The rate itself matches the key exactly (9% per annum IRR, compounded annually, hard hurdle). However, the answer omits two elements the key treats as part of this term: the basis of the preferred return (accrued on Capital Contributions) and the GP catch-up structure (50/50 catch-up until the GP has received 20% of profits). The catch-up in particular is a substantive component of how the hurdle operates, not merely extra colour, so the answer is incomplete rather than a differently-worded match.
